nodes.summary: If $a$ and $b$ are distinct complex numbers with $|a| = |b| = 1$, then $|a + b| < 2$.
nodes.title: Sum of two distinct unit complex numbers

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite multiset of complex numbers, each of absolute value $1$, containing two distinct elements. Then the absolute value of the sum of $s$ is strictly less than the number of elements of $s$, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Strict triangle inequality for unit complex numbers, multiset form

nodes.summary: Let $\mu_1, \dots, \mu_n$ be complex numbers with $|\mu_i| = 1$ for every $i$, not all equal. Then $\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n} \mu_i\right| < n$.
nodes.title: Strict triangle inequality for unit complex numbers

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g \in G$ satisfies $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$, then any two roots of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ are equal.
nodes.title: Characters of full absolute value have equal eigenvalues

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$, then $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$ or $\chi(g) = 0$.
nodes.title: Burnside's vanishing theorem for coprime class sizes

nodes.summary: Suppose that every finite simple group $H$ having an element $h \ne 1$ whose conjugacy class has size $r^k$ for some prime $r$ and some $k \ge 1$ has prime order. Then for all primes $p$ and $q$ and all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, every finite group $G$ of order $p^a q^b$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem from the prime-power class corollary

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group whose underlying type lies in the lowest type universe, let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers. If $G$ has order $p^a q^b$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem in the lowest universe

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers. If $G$ has order $p^a q^b$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Every finite set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ has at most $|G|$ elements.
nodes.title: Bound on the number of irreducible representations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple group and let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of dimension $1$. If the character of $\rho$ is not the constant function $1$, then the order of $G$ is a prime number.
nodes.title: A simple group with a nontrivial linear character has prime order

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For every conjugacy class $K$ of $G$, the set of elements of $K$ equals the conjugacy class of the chosen representative of $K$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy class of the chosen representative

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For every conjugacy class $C$ of $G$, the complex number $\omega_\rho(C)$ by which the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ acts on $V$ is an algebraic integer, that is, integral over $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Central scalars are algebraic integers

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. Fix a representative $g_C$ of each conjugacy class $C$. For conjugacy classes $C_1$ and $C_2$,
nodes.title: Central scalars multiply via the class structure constants

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with character $\chi$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. Then $\omega_\rho(C) \cdot \dim V = \sum_{x \in C} \chi(x)$.
nodes.title: Trace formula for central scalars

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For a conjugacy class $C$ of $G$, the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ is central in the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, so it acts on $V$ as multiplication by a complex number. The central scalar $\omega_\rho(C)$ is that number: $\rho\bigl(\sum_{x \in C} x\bigr) v = \omega_\rho(C)\, v$ for all $v \in V$.
nodes.title: Central scalar of a conjugacy class

nodes.summary: For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, this is the bijection from the centralizer $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ onto the stabilizer of $g$ for the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, that sends each element $x$ to itself.
nodes.title: Centralizer as a conjugation stabilizer

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with $\dim V > 1$. Then the scalar center of $\rho$ is a proper subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: The scalar center of a nonlinear irreducible representation is proper

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. The scalar center of $\rho$ is the subgroup of $G$ consisting of the elements $g$ such that $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Scalar center of a representation

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$, then $\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.
nodes.title: Integrality of the normalized character value at a coprime class

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g_l$ be the chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then $\chi(x) = \chi(g_l)$ for every $x \in l$.
nodes.title: Characters are constant on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$ and $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then $\chi(g) = 0$.
nodes.title: Character vanishing from coprimality and a strict norm bound

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an isomorphism class of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with chosen representative $(V, \rho)$. For every $x \in G$, the character of $c$ at $x$ equals the character of the representation $\rho$ at $x$, namely $\operatorname{tr} \rho(x)$.
nodes.title: Character of a class via its chosen representative

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Two isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ that have the same character are equal.
nodes.title: Characters determine irreducible representations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an isomorphism class of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. The character of $c$ at the identity $1 \in G$ equals the dimension over $\mathbb{C}$ of the chosen representative of $c$.
nodes.title: Character value at the identity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The character of the isomorphism class of the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{C}$ takes the value $1$ at every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Character of the trivial representation

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. For an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, the character of $c$ is the function $\chi_c \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $\chi_c(g) = \operatorname{tr} \rho(g)$ for any representative $(V, \rho)$ of $c$. It does not depend on the representative, since isomorphic representations have the same character.
nodes.title: Character of an isomorphism class

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\chi_i$ and $\chi_j$ be the characters of isomorphism classes $i$ and $j$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. Then
nodes.title: Orthogonality of irreducible characters

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g_l$ be the chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then $\chi(x^{-1}) = \chi(g_l^{-1})$ for every $x \in l$.
nodes.title: Characters at inverses are constant on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$ have finite order $m$. Then $\chi(g)$ lies in the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity.
nodes.title: Character values lie in a cyclotomic field

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ has two distinct roots.
nodes.title: Characteristic roots are not all equal below the degree

nodes.summary: Nonlinear irreducible characters of a simple group vanish on nonidentity classes of coprime size. Let $G$ be a finite simple group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ of dimension $d > 1$, and let $\chi$ be the character of $\rho$. If $g \ne 1$ is an element of $G$ whose conjugacy class has size coprime to $d$, then $\chi(g) = 0$.
nodes.title: Nonlinear irreducible characters of a simple group vanish on nonidentity classes of coprime size

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. Then $\chi(g)$ is the sum of the roots of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Character value as the sum of characteristic roots

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then $\chi(g)$ is an algebraic integer for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Character values are algebraic integers

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$. For every $g \in G$, every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $|\mu| = 1$.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a finite group representation have modulus one

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, and $g \in G$ an element of order $n$, where $n = 0$ if $g$ has infinite order. Then every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^n = 1$; in particular, when $g$ has finite order, $\mu$ is a root of unity.
nodes.title: Characteristic roots are killed by the order of the element

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$ and $g \in G$. The characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ has exactly $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ roots in $\mathbb{C}$, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Number of characteristic roots of a representation matrix

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$. For a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$, let $g_l$ be its chosen representative and $\omega(l)$ the central scalar of $l$, the scalar by which the class sum of $l$ acts on $V$. Then $\sum_{x \in l} \chi(x)\chi(x^{-1}) = (\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V)\,\omega(l)\,\chi(g_l^{-1})$.
nodes.title: Contribution of a conjugacy class to the self-pairing sum

nodes.summary: For each conjugacy class $K$ of a group $G$, the representative of $K$ is an element $g_K \in G$, fixed once and for all by choice, whose conjugacy class is $K$.
nodes.title: Chosen representative of a conjugacy class

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For every conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ and every element $w$ of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, the class sum $\widehat{K} = \sum_{x \in K} x$ satisfies $w \widehat{K} = \widehat{K} w$.
nodes.title: Class sums of conjugacy classes are central

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g \in G$, and let $\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then $w \widehat{C_g} = \widehat{C_g} w$ for every $w \in \mathbb{C}[G]$.
nodes.title: The class sum of the conjugacy class of an element is central

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$. For every $g \in G$, if $C$ is the conjugacy class of $g$, then $|C|\,\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.
nodes.title: Class size times character ratio is an algebraic integer

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g \in G$, and let $\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then $\widehat{C_g} h = h \widehat{C_g}$ for every $h \in G$, where $h$ is viewed as a basis element of $\mathbb{C}[G]$.
nodes.title: Class sums commute with group elements

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For a finite subset $C$ of $G$ write $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, and for $g \in G$ let $C_g$ be its conjugacy class. Let $g_i, g_j \in G$, and for each conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ with chosen representative $z_K$ let $a_K$ be the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_{g_i} \times C_{g_j}$ with $x y = z_K$. Then…
nodes.title: Products of class sums expand in class sums

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. The class sum of a finite subset $C \subseteq G$ is the element $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$.
nodes.title: Class sum of a finite subset

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a class function, that is, $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Suppose that for every isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with character $\chi_c$,
nodes.title: Class functions orthogonal to all irreducible characters vanish

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a class function, and for each of the finitely many isomorphism classes $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ let $\chi_c$ be its character. Then
nodes.title: Expansion of class functions in irreducible characters

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $C_i$ and $C_j$ be finite subsets of $G$, and write $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$. For every $u \in G$, the coefficient of $u$ in $\widehat{C_i} \widehat{C_j}$ is the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $x y = u$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of a product of class sums

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an element of a finite group $G$, let $g^G$ be its conjugacy class and let $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ be its centralizer. Then $|g^G| \cdot |C_G(g)| = |G|$.
nodes.title: Class size times centralizer order

nodes.summary: For every element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ times the order of the stabilizer of $g$ under the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, equals the order of $G$.
nodes.title: Orbit–stabilizer for a conjugacy class

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. If $g_1, g_2 \in G$ are conjugate, then the conjugacy class of $g_1$ equals the conjugacy class of $g_2$.
nodes.title: Conjugate elements have the same conjugacy class

nodes.summary: For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the conjugacy class of $g$ is the finite set $\{h g h^{-1} : h \in G\}$, the orbit of $g$ under the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation.
nodes.title: Conjugacy class

nodes.summary: Let $g$, $h$ and $x$ be elements of a finite group $G$. If $x$ lies in the conjugacy class of $g$, then so does $h x h^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy classes are closed under conjugation

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $g \in G$ be such that every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^m = 1$. Each such root $\mu$ is regarded as an element of the subfield $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ obtained by adjoining the $m$-th roots of unity to $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.title: Characteristic roots as elements of the cyclotomic field

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be a conjugacy class of a finite group $G$ and $g_l$ its chosen representative. For every $x \in l$ there is $c \in G$ with $c x c^{-1} = g_l$.
nodes.title: Members of a conjugacy class are conjugate to its representative

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple group and let $g \ne 1$ be an element of $G$ whose conjugacy class has size $r^k$ for some prime $r$ and some $k \ge 1$. Then the order of $G$ is a prime number.
nodes.title: A simple group with a prime-power conjugacy class has prime order

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m \neq 0$, the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity is a splitting field over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the polynomial $X^m - 1 \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$.
nodes.title: The $m$-th cyclotomic field is a splitting field of $X^m - 1$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m \neq 0$, the set of complex roots of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ is exactly the set of $m$-th roots of unity in $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Complex roots of $X^m - 1$

nodes.summary: For $m = 0$ the cyclotomic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is the bottom intermediate field, that is $\mathbb{Q}$ itself: the polynomial $X^0 - 1$ is zero and is taken to have no roots, so nothing is adjoined.
nodes.title: The zeroth cyclotomic field is $\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, the $m$-th cyclotomic field is the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{Q}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity, that is, by the complex roots of $X^m - 1$.
nodes.title: Cyclotomic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ divides $|G|$.
nodes.title: Degrees of irreducible representations divide the group order

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\delta \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be the indicator function of the identity, so $\delta(1) = 1$ and $\delta(g) = 0$ for $g \neq 1$, and let $\chi_c$ be the character of an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. Then
nodes.title: Pairing of the identity indicator with a character

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, $\delta_1 \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the function with $\delta_1(1) = 1$ and $\delta_1(g) = 0$ for every $g \ne 1$.
nodes.title: Delta function at the identity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with character $\chi$, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $g \in G$ be such that every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^m = 1$. Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be the field obtained by adjoining the $m$-th roots of unity to $\mathbb{Q}$, and suppose $\chi(g) \in K$. Then for…
nodes.title: Field embeddings applied to character values

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|b| = 1$. If $a \bar{b} = 1$, then $a = b$.
nodes.title: Cancelling a unit-modulus conjugate

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers. Every natural number $d$ dividing $p^a q^b$ has the form $d = p^{a'} q^{b'}$ for some natural numbers $a'$ and $b'$.
nodes.title: Divisors of $p^a q^b$

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, $g \in G$ and $\mu_0 \in \mathbb{C}$. If every root of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ equals $\mu_0$, then $\rho(g) = \mu_0 \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.
nodes.title: Elements with a single eigenvalue act as scalars

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of dimension $1$, and let $\chi$ be the character of $\rho$. Then for every $g \in G$ the operator $\rho(g)$ is multiplication by the scalar $\chi(g)$, that is, $\rho(g) = \chi(g) \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.
nodes.title: One-dimensional representations act by their character

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.
nodes.title: Elements of the scalar center act by scalars

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be primes, let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $b \ge 1$, and let $G$ be a finite group of order $p^a q^b$. Then there are an element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ and a natural number $k \le a$ such that the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements.
nodes.title: A nontrivial element whose class size is a power of $p$

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, extended linearly to the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$. If $z \in \mathbb{C}[G]$ commutes with every element of $\mathbb{C}[G]$, then $z$ acts on $V$ as a scalar: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\rho(z) v = c\, v$ for all $v \in V$.
nodes.title: Schur's lemma for central elements of the group algebra

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number. There is no algebraic integer $\beta \in \mathbb{C}$ with $1 + p\beta = 0$, since such a $\beta$ would make $-1/p$ an algebraic integer.
nodes.title: An algebraic integer cannot solve $1 + p\beta = 0$ for a prime $p$

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, $\mathrm{Irr}(G)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism classes of simple representations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $V$ a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. If $\sigma$ is a representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ that equals the action of $G$ on $V$, then $\sigma$ is irreducible.
nodes.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations are irreducible (auxiliary form)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. If $V$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, then the representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ is irreducible.
nodes.title: Simple finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group are irreducible

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ on a finite group $G$ is a class function when $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$, that is, when $f$ is constant on conjugacy classes.
nodes.title: Class function

nodes.summary: Every finite group whose order is a prime number is solvable.
nodes.title: Groups of prime order are solvable

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, two simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ are related when they are isomorphic; this is an equivalence relation on the simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism of simple representations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of dimension $1$, with character $\chi$. This is the group homomorphism from $G$ to the multiplicative group $\mathbb{C}^\times$ of nonzero complex numbers that sends $g$ to $\chi(g)$.
nodes.title: A linear character as a homomorphism to $\mathbb{C}^\times$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$, mapping the coefficients of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ along the inclusion $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{C}$ gives the complex polynomial $X^m - 1$.
nodes.title: $X^m - 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and over $\mathbb{C}$

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. An element $g \in G$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$ if and only if $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Membership in the scalar center

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g \in G$ and $c \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$, then $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$.
nodes.title: Elements acting by a scalar lie in the scalar center

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$.
nodes.title: Elements of the scalar center have character of full absolute value

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $b$ with $|a| = |b| = 1$, we have $|a \bar{b}| = 1$.
nodes.title: Product of a unit complex number with a conjugate unit

nodes.summary: If $w \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfies $|w| = 1$ and $w \neq 1$, then $\operatorname{Re} w < 1$.
nodes.title: Real part of a unit complex number other than $1$

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $b$, $\operatorname{Re} a \operatorname{Re} b + \operatorname{Im} a \operatorname{Im} b = \operatorname{Re}(a \bar{b})$.
nodes.title: Real part of a product with a conjugate

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its character. For every $g \in G$ with $g \ne 1$, $\sum_c \chi_c(1)\,\chi_c(g) = 0$, where the sum runs over all such classes $c$.
nodes.title: Column orthogonality at the identity

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$ and an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, this is a simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ in the class $c$, fixed by the axiom of choice.
nodes.title: Chosen representative of an isomorphism class

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $S_\rho$ be the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the class sums of the conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. If $a, b \in S_\rho$, then $ab$ lies in the $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$.
nodes.title: Products of central-scalar generators stay in their span

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. The set $S_\rho$ is the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the values $\omega_\rho(C)$ for all conjugacy classes $C$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Generators of the central-scalar ring

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $S_\rho$ be the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the class sums of the conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. The $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$ is closed under multiplication, and this is that span as a $\mathbb{Z}$-subalgebra of $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Ring generated by the central scalars

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then $\sum_{g \in G} \chi(g)\chi(g^{-1}) = |G|$.
nodes.title: Self-orthogonality of an irreducible character

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $\sigma$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then $V$ with the action $\sigma$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.
nodes.title: Irreducible representations are simple

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g_i, g_j \in G$ with conjugacy classes $C_{g_i}$ and $C_{g_j}$, and for $z \in G$ let $a(z)$ be the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_{g_i} \times C_{g_j}$ with $x y = z$. If $u, z \in G$ are conjugate, then $a(u) = a(z)$.
nodes.title: Class structure constants are class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For finite subsets $C_i, C_j \subseteq G$ and an element $z \in G$, the structure constant is the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $xy = z$.
nodes.title: Structure constants of a pair of subsets

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its character. Then $\sum_c \chi_c(1)^2 = |G|$, where the sum runs over all such classes $c$.
nodes.title: Sum of squared degrees

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$ and every function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $\sum_{g \in G} f(g) = \sum_{l} \sum_{x \in l} f(x)$, where $l$ runs over the conjugacy classes of $G$.
nodes.title: Splitting a sum over conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{C}$, where every element of $G$ acts as the identity, is simple, and this is its class among the isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.
nodes.title: The trivial irreducible class

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M$ be a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module structure, and write $\rho(h)$ for the action of $h \in G$ on $M$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is a class function, then its averaging operator $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$ satisfies $\rho(h)(T_f x) = T_f(\rho(h) x)$ for all $h \in G$ and $x \in M$.
nodes.title: The averaging operator of a class function is $G$-equivariant

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M$ be a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module structure, and write $\rho(g)$ for the action of $g \in G$ on $M$. For a function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, the averaging operator of $f$ is the $\mathbb{C}$-linear endomorphism $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$ of $M$.
nodes.title: Zimmerman's averaging operator

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
